availability.note: GWM AU configurator data (/au/config/tank-300/_payload.json) lists 'TANK 300 Lux PHEV' with driveaway_retail_price; model page https://www.gwmanz.com/au/models/suv/tank-300/ shows Lux PHEV and Ultra PHEV in the range carousel and JSON-LD 'Lux PHEV / Ultra PHEV'. Two PHEV grades, matching CarExpert and Chasing Cars.

listPrice.note: GWM publishes drive-away only. Configurator data: driveaway_retail_price 57990.00 (ABN 56990.00), 'Price applicable for 2026 build vehicle', VIC private buyer basis per GWM offers page; the only November offer on PHEV grades is 0.88% finance, no drive-away discount, so this is the standard price (launch $2,000 lower ended 1 June 2026). Also CarExpert long-term review 22 Sep 2026 and Chasing Cars. Passenger divisor: (57990 - 958.80) / 1.042 = 54,732; round-trip through calc/onroad.js driveAwayPrice (isNonPassenger false) = 57,989.94. Check against figures GWM did not choose for this grade: the same back-out applied to GWM's standard diesel drive-aways reproduces CarsGuide/RedBook diesel MSRPs within $19-181 (Lux diesel 48,990 -> 46,171 vs 46,190), so GWM drive-away is list + VIC on-roads. CarsGuide/RedBook PHEV 'MSRP' of 55990 equals the expired launch drive-away exactly (a list of that size would cost ~59,222 on the road in VIC), so it is a copied drive-away figure and was rejected, as was the held row's 55990. Re-derived 2026-11-27 for VIC rego $958.80 (was 54,808 at $880; round trip 57989.54).

batteryKwh.note: '37.11kWh nickel manganese cobalt (NMC)'; also EV Central spec table, carsales 37.1. Chasing Cars labels 37.1kWh gross; usable unpublished. Chinese market moved to a 36.7kWh CATL pack in Dec 2025 but AU sources through Sep 2026 still quote 37.11. Same unlabelled treatment as Cannon Alpha / Tank 500.

rangeKm.note: GWM AU 'Up to 115km electric driving range (NEDC)'; carsales 'Electric Driving Range km (ADR)' 115. No manufacturer WLTP exists: GWM does not sell this Hi4-T in the UK/EU (held research checked gwmcars.co.uk). Chasing Cars quotes '100km ... WLTP' without a source and the Chinese CLTC figure is 105km; not used. Testers: Chasing Cars 85-95km stop-start, EV Central ~90km.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 37.11 / 115 x 100 = 32.27. CarExpert's 'claimed energy consumption 27.2kWh/100km' is the ADR label figure, which field rules bar for a PHEV; not used. Tautological against the cross-check.

combinedRangeKm.note: rangeKm + tank / fuelConsumptionL100km x 100 = 115 + 70 / 8.3 x 100 = 958. Tank 70L per CarExpert price-and-specs, EV Central spec table, Chasing Cars and carsales (CarExpert long-term review says 75L, outvoted; 75L is the Cannon ute's tank). GWM's own NEDC total is 955km, consistent with 70L and 8.3.

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: GWM's published 'low-charge' (charge-sustaining) figure 8.3L/100km, also in EV Central's spec table and CarExpert long-term review. GWM convention across Cannon (8.1, derived from GWM total-range claim), Cannon Alpha (7.9) and Tank 500 (8.4): use GWM's own figure. Real-world is worse: CarsGuide 11.0 urban / 8.5 country, Chasing Cars up to 10 in town, EV Central over 12 on the freeway.

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: Combined-cycle label 1.9L/100km (NEDC), at or below 3.5. Also carsales 'Fuel Consumption Combined 1.9'.

isGreenForVicDuty.note: SRO: green cars are passenger cars with combined CO2 of 120 g/km or less; carsales lists 'CO2 Emission Combined 43 g/km' (https://www.carsales.com.au/research/gwm/tank-300/2026/ultra-hi4-t-phev/). Passenger SUV, not a ute.

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: '360 litres with rear seats up'; same in Chasing Cars and carsales 'Boot / Load Space Min 360'. Measurement method (to cover vs roof) not stated by any source; GWM AU pages publish no boot figure.

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: '1520 litres with rear seats folded'; Chasing Cars and carsales agree. Method unstated.

seats.note: 'Seat Capacity 5'; GWM model page JSON-LD seatingCapacity 5.

towKg.note: GWM AU '3,000kg braked towing capacity'; CarExpert 3000kg braked / 750kg unbraked.

warrantyYears.note: GWM AU '7-year unlimited kilometre warranty', no servicing condition; CarExpert long-term: battery 8 years unlimited km.

insuranceAnnual.note: Kept held value; anchored to byd-shark-6-premium (1800 at $57,900 list) and gwm-cannon-phev-ultra (1800 at $52,687); slightly higher for a 300kW 2.6t off-road SUV. Cannon Alpha Lux sits at 1900 at $59,990.

depreciationCurve.note: One curve per brand (owner convention): the GWM curve used by gwm-cannon-phev and gwm-cannon-alpha-phev; replaces the held Tank 300-specific [1,0.71,0.6,0.51,0.44,0.38]. Evidence for below-mainstream retention: launch price raised $2,000 then finance campaigns, brand-wide rolling drive-away discounts, a Chinese-market 59.6kWh Tank 300L successor already public.

gwm-tank-300-phev-lux.fuelConsumptionL100km: GWM's 8.3 low-charge figure against real-world 8.5-12+ L/100km, so running cost is likely understated (same for Ultra)
gwm-tank-300-phev-lux.combinedRangeKm: computed from NEDC range and GWM 8.3; tank 70L vs one 75L citation (same for Ultra)
gwm-tank-300-phev-lux.batteryKwh: 37.11 unlabelled (Chasing Cars says gross), usable unknown; consumption derived from it (same for Ultra)
gwm-tank-300-phev-lux.listPrice: backed out of GWM VIC private drive-away $57,990; verified only indirectly via the diesel grades' RedBook MSRPs
gwm-tank-300-phev-ultra.listPrice: backed out of $61,990 drive-away, same caveat
gwm-tank-300-phev-lux.bootLitresSeatsUp: 360/1520 measurement method unstated, may not be to the cargo cover (same for SeatsDown and Ultra)
gwm-tank-300-phev-lux.insuranceAnnual: judged against Shark 6 and Cannon siblings
